coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy Z2 only—8–10 miles at 140–150 bpm, no faster. Your recovery score is 38/100 and resting HR is 6.5 bpm above your 30-day average; your body is still paying down a debt. You've dropped from 30.2 miles last week to 17.2 so far this week, which is correct for taper, but the quality of that recovery matters more than volume right now. Keep it conversational, focus on leg turnover and smooth breathing. You're 53 days out—sharpness will return once you sleep and stabilize.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You logged 6.89 hours of sleep at 87.4% efficiency last night—that's a deficit. Prioritize carbs today (aim for 6–7g per kg of body weight across the day) to replenish glycogen and support nervous system recovery. In an easy run like today's, you won't need gels, but post-run, get 30–40g protein + 80–100g carbs within 30 minutes. Your elevated resting HR suggests glycogen depletion or sleep debt; carbohydrate is the fastest lever to pull before Tuesday's potential quality session.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep is your bottleneck right now—you're at 6.89h vs. your 30-day average of 8.24h, a 1.35-hour shortfall. Tonight, aim for 9 hours in a cool, dark room; skip the work email after 8 PM. If travel is causing the sleep loss, that's a conversation we need—you cannot taper effectively on six-hour nights. Active recovery (easy run today) is fine, but passive recovery (sleep, zero work stress) is what unlocks the adaptation you've built over 26 weeks.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're in the mental hardest part of taper—reduced volume can feel like detraining, especially for a high-output executive. It isn't. The Julian Alps 50K is an 8–10 hour alpine grind with sparse aid; that demands a fresh nervous system and full glycogen stores, both of which need 7 weeks of genuine recovery layered into your taper. Trust the phase. Easy runs, sleep, and fuel are not soft—they're the final loadbearing walls before race day.
